steps.message:
# Agentic RL tool-call parser diagnosis

Review the staged public Miles + Harbor + mini-swe-agent historical snapshot.
Inspect the launch configuration, model and parser settings, TITO-v2 session
metadata, rollout records, and frozen run metrics.

Do not launch another training run, start SGLang, create sandboxes, download a
model or dataset, use the network, or modify the historical snapshot.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the health verdict, identify the concrete configuration root cause, and
explain the causal chain from that setting through the observed session
mismatches to the training-leaf accounting. Quote the exact logical-rollout,
training-leaf, inflation, fan-out, and mismatch values from the frozen metrics.
Distinguish the configuration defect from any separate residual MiniSWE
behavior; do not merge them into one unproven root cause.
I'll start by exploring the workspace to understand the snapshot structure.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run one normal 8-GPU Miles/Harbor GRPO update and summarize the observation.
3	set -euo pipefail
4	
5	WS="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
6	: "${AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED:=$WS/.prepared}"
7	: "${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:=/tmp/autorlbench-results}"
8	mkdir -p "$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs"
9	
10	if [ -f "$AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED/env" ]; then
11	  set -a
12	  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
13	  source "$AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED/env"
14	  set +a
15	fi
16	
17	: "${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH to the Qwen3-30B-A3B HF checkpoint}"
18	: "${SESSION_SERVER_EXTERNAL_HOST:?set SESSION_SERVER_EXTERNAL_HOST to a host the sandboxes can reach}"
19	: "${HARBOR_ENV_TYPE:=e2b}"
20	: "${SANDBOX_BACKEND:=tencent_ags}"
21	: "${MILES_SOURCE_DIR:?MILES_SOURCE_DIR is written by environment/prepare.sh}"
22	: "${MEGATRON_PATH:?MEGATRON_PATH is written by environment/prepare.sh}"
23	: "${MILES_MODEL_BASE:=$AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED/models}"
24	: "${MODEL_NAME:=Qwen3-30B-A3B-autorlbench}"
25	: "${MILES_PROMPT_DATA:=$WS/data/miles_prompts.jsonl}"
26	: "${HARBOR_TASKS_DIR:=$WS/harbor_tasks}"
27	: "${HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR:=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/harbor_trials}"
28	: "${MILES_DUMP_DIR:=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/dump_details}"
29	: "${MILES_HOST_IP:=0.0.0.0}"
30	: "${EXPECTED_LOGICAL_ROLLOUTS:=64}"
31	: "${RUN_MODE:=normal}"
32	
33	if [ "$HARBOR_ENV_TYPE" != "e2b" ]; then
34	  echo "[run] this package currently expects HARBOR_ENV_TYPE=e2b; got $HARBOR_ENV_TYPE" >&2
35	  exit 2
36	fi
37	
38	if [ "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" != "tencent_ags" ] && [ "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" != "e2b" ]; then
39	  echo "[run] SANDBOX_BACKEND must be tencent_ags or e2b; got $SANDBOX_BACKEND" >&2
40	  exit 2
41	fi
42	
43	if [ "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" = "tencent_ags" ]; then
44	  : "${TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE:?set TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE to the fixed Tencent AGS template}"
45	  if [ -n "${TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN:-}" ]; then
46	    E2B_DOMAIN="${E2B_DOMAIN:-$TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN}"
47	    export E2B_DOMAIN
48	  fi
49	  if [ -n "${TENCENT_AGS_URL:-}" ]; then
50	    E2B_API_URL="${E2B_API_URL:-$TENCENT_AGS_URL}"
51	    export E2B_API_URL
52	  fi
53	  if [ -z "${E2B_API_URL:-}" ] && [ -n "${E2B_DOMAIN:-}" ]; then
54	    E2B_API_URL="https://api.${E2B_DOMAIN}"
55	    export E2B_API_URL
56	  fi
57	  if [ -z "${E2B_DOMAIN:-}" ] && [ -z "${E2B_SANDBOX_URL:-}" ]; then
58	    echo "[run] Tencent AGS needs TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN (or E2B_SANDBOX_URL for a custom data plane)" >&2
59	    exit 2
60	  fi
61	  : "${TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE:=enterprise}"
62	  : "${TENCENT_AGS_FORCE_HTTP1:=0}"
63	  : "${TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR:?set TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR to a Python 3.10 wheelhouse tar.gz}"
64	  export TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE
65	  export TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REWRITE="${TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REWRITE:-}"
66	  export TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE
67	  export TENCENT_AGS_FORCE_HTTP1
68	  export TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR
69	fi
70	
71	TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE=""
72	cleanup() {
73	  if [ -n "$TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE" ] && [ -f "$TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE" ]; then
74	    rm -f "$TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE"
75	  fi
76	  ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
77	}
78	trap cleanup EXIT
79	
80	if [ -n "${E2B_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
81	  if [ -z "${E2B_API_KEY_FILE:-}" ]; then
82	    E2B_API_KEY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/miles-miniswe-e2b-key.XXXXXX")"
83	    TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE="$E2B_API_KEY_FILE"
84	  fi
85	  if [ ! -s "$E2B_API_KEY_FILE" ]; then
86	    printf '%s\n' "$E2B_API_KEY" > "$E2B_API_KEY_FILE"
87	    chmod 600 "$E2B_API_KEY_FILE"
88	  fi
89	  export E2B_API_KEY_FILE
90	  unset E2B_API_KEY
91	fi
92	
93	if [ -z "${E2B_API_KEY:-}" ] && [ -z "${E2B_API_KEY_FILE:-}" ]; then
94	  echo "[run] set E2B_API_KEY or E2B_API_KEY_FILE for the E2B-compatible sandbox" >&2
95	  exit 2
96	fi
97	
98	export HARBOR_ENV_TYPE
99	export HARBOR_TASKS_DIR
100	export HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR
101	export AGENT_MODEL_NAME=model
102	export AGENT_TIMEOUT=5400
103	export AGENT_TRIAL_TIMEOUT=7200
104	export AGENT_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=28672
105	export AGENT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096
106	export HARBOR_MAX_SEQ_LEN=32768
107	export MILES_HOST_IP
108	export MILES_DUMP_DIR
109	export EXPECTED_LOGICAL_ROLLOUTS
110	export PYTHONPATH="$WS:$MILES_SOURCE_DIR:$MILES_SOURCE_DIR/examples/experimental/harbor:$MILES_SOURCE_DIR/examples/swe-agent-harbor-docker${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
111	
112	skip_prepare_args=()
113	if [ "${MILES_SKIP_PREPARE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
114	  skip_prepare_args=(--skip-prepare)
115	fi
116	
117	mkdir -p "$MILES_DUMP_DIR" "$HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR"
118	driver_log="$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/driver_$(date -u +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log"
119	
120	set +e
121	python3 "$WS/run_miles.py" \
122	  --mode "$RUN_MODE" \
123	  --sandbox-backend "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" \
124	  --num-gpus-per-node 8 \
125	  --megatron-path "$MEGATRON_PATH" \
126	  --base-dir "$MILES_MODEL_BASE" \
127	  --model-name "$MODEL_NAME" \
128	  --hf-checkpoint "$MODEL_PATH" \
129	  --prompt-data "$MILES_PROMPT_DATA" \
130	  --save-traces-dir "$MILES_DUMP_DIR" \
131	  --harbor-tasks-dir "$HARBOR_TASKS_DIR" \
132	  --harbor-trials-dir "$HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR" \
133	  "${skip_prepare_args[@]}" \
134	  2>&1 | tee "$driver_log"
135	STATUS="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
136	set -e
137	
138	python3 "$WS/summarize_run.py"
139	SUMMARY_STATUS=$?
140	
141	if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then
142	  exit "$STATUS"
143	fi
144	exit "$SUMMARY_STATUS"
145

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run one normal 8-GPU Miles/Harbor GRPO update and summarize the observation.
set -euo pipefail

WS="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
: "${AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED:=$WS/.prepared}"
: "${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:=/tmp/autorlbench-results}"
mkdir -p "$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs"

if [ -f "$AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED/env" ]; then
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  source "$AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED/env"
  set +a
fi

: "${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH to the Qwen3-30B-A3B HF checkpoint}"
: "${SESSION_SERVER_EXTERNAL_HOST:?set SESSION_SERVER_EXTERNAL_HOST to a host the sandboxes can reach}"
: "${HARBOR_ENV_TYPE:=e2b}"
: "${SANDBOX_BACKEND:=tencent_ags}"
: "${MILES_SOURCE_DIR:?MILES_SOURCE_DIR is written by environment/prepare.sh}"
: "${MEGATRON_PATH:?MEGATRON_PATH is written by environment/prepare.sh}"
: "${MILES_MODEL_BASE:=$AUTORLBENCH_PREPARED/models}"
: "${MODEL_NAME:=Qwen3-30B-A3B-autorlbench}"
: "${MILES_PROMPT_DATA:=$WS/data/miles_prompts.jsonl}"
: "${HARBOR_TASKS_DIR:=$WS/harbor_tasks}"
: "${HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR:=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/harbor_trials}"
: "${MILES_DUMP_DIR:=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/dump_details}"
: "${MILES_HOST_IP:=0.0.0.0}"
: "${EXPECTED_LOGICAL_ROLLOUTS:=64}"
: "${RUN_MODE:=normal}"

if [ "$HARBOR_ENV_TYPE" != "e2b" ]; then
  echo "[run] this package currently expects HARBOR_ENV_TYPE=e2b; got $HARBOR_ENV_TYPE" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [ "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" != "tencent_ags" ] && [ "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" != "e2b" ]; then
  echo "[run] SANDBOX_BACKEND must be tencent_ags or e2b; got $SANDBOX_BACKEND" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [ "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" = "tencent_ags" ]; then
  : "${TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE:?set TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE to the fixed Tencent AGS template}"
  if [ -n "${TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN:-}" ]; then
    E2B_DOMAIN="${E2B_DOMAIN:-$TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN}"
    export E2B_DOMAIN
  fi
  if [ -n "${TENCENT_AGS_URL:-}" ]; then
    E2B_API_URL="${E2B_API_URL:-$TENCENT_AGS_URL}"
    export E2B_API_URL
  fi
  if [ -z "${E2B_API_URL:-}" ] && [ -n "${E2B_DOMAIN:-}" ]; then
    E2B_API_URL="https://api.${E2B_DOMAIN}"
    export E2B_API_URL
  fi
  if [ -z "${E2B_DOMAIN:-}" ] && [ -z "${E2B_SANDBOX_URL:-}" ]; then
    echo "[run] Tencent AGS needs TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN (or E2B_SANDBOX_URL for a custom data plane)" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  : "${TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE:=enterprise}"
  : "${TENCENT_AGS_FORCE_HTTP1:=0}"
  : "${TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR:?set TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR to a Python 3.10 wheelhouse tar.gz}"
  export TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE
  export TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REWRITE="${TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REWRITE:-}"
  export TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE
  export TENCENT_AGS_FORCE_HTTP1
  export TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR
fi

TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE=""
cleanup() {
  if [ -n "$TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE" ] && [ -f "$TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE" ]; then
    rm -f "$TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE"
  fi
  ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

if [ -n "${E2B_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  if [ -z "${E2B_API_KEY_FILE:-}" ]; then
    E2B_API_KEY_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/miles-miniswe-e2b-key.XXXXXX")"
    TEMP_E2B_KEY_FILE="$E2B_API_KEY_FILE"
  fi
  if [ ! -s "$E2B_API_KEY_FILE" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$E2B_API_KEY" > "$E2B_API_KEY_FILE"
    chmod 600 "$E2B_API_KEY_FILE"
  fi
  export E2B_API_KEY_FILE
  unset E2B_API_KEY
fi

if [ -z "${E2B_API_KEY:-}" ] && [ -z "${E2B_API_KEY_FILE:-}" ]; then
  echo "[run] set E2B_API_KEY or E2B_API_KEY_FILE for the E2B-compatible sandbox" >&2
  exit 2
fi

export HARBOR_ENV_TYPE
export HARBOR_TASKS_DIR
export HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR
export AGENT_MODEL_NAME=model
export AGENT_TIMEOUT=5400
export AGENT_TRIAL_TIMEOUT=7200
export AGENT_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=28672
export AGENT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096
export HARBOR_MAX_SEQ_LEN=32768
export MILES_HOST_IP
export MILES_DUMP_DIR
export EXPECTED_LOGICAL_ROLLOUTS
export PYTHONPATH="$WS:$MILES_SOURCE_DIR:$MILES_SOURCE_DIR/examples/experimental/harbor:$MILES_SOURCE_DIR/examples/swe-agent-harbor-docker${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

skip_prepare_args=()
if [ "${MILES_SKIP_PREPARE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  skip_prepare_args=(--skip-prepare)
fi

mkdir -p "$MILES_DUMP_DIR" "$HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR"
driver_log="$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/driver_$(date -u +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log"

set +e
python3 "$WS/run_miles.py" \
  --mode "$RUN_MODE" \
  --sandbox-backend "$SANDBOX_BACKEND" \
  --num-gpus-per-node 8 \
  --megatron-path "$MEGATRON_PATH" \
  --base-dir "$MILES_MODEL_BASE" \
  --model-name "$MODEL_NAME" \
  --hf-checkpoint "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --prompt-data "$MILES_PROMPT_DATA" \
  --save-traces-dir "$MILES_DUMP_DIR" \
  --harbor-tasks-dir "$HARBOR_TASKS_DIR" \
  --harbor-trials-dir "$HARBOR_TRIALS_DIR" \
  "${skip_prepare_args[@]}" \
  2>&1 | tee "$driver_log"
STATUS="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
set -e

python3 "$WS/summarize_run.py"
SUMMARY_STATUS=$?

if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit "$STATUS"
fi
exit "$SUMMARY_STATUS"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Launch the Miles + Harbor + mini-swe-agent GRPO observation run."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

import typer

from launch_common import agentic_pythonpath_dirs, harbor_env_vars
from miles.utils.external_utils import command_utils


@dataclass
class ScriptArgs(command_utils.ExecuteTrainConfig):
    mode: Literal["normal", "debug_rollout_only"] = "normal"
    run_id: str = command_utils.create_run_id()
    megatron_model_type: str = "qwen3-30B-A3B"
    num_gpus_per_node: int = 8
    megatron_path: str = os.environ.get("MEGATRON_PATH", "/root/Megatron-LM")

    skip_prepare: bool = False
    base_dir: str = os.environ.get("MILES_MODEL_BASE", "/tmp/models")

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.hf_checkpoint:
            raise ValueError("set MODEL_PATH or --hf-checkpoint")

            self.harbor_tasks_dir = str(Path(__file__).with_name("harbor_tasks"))
        if not self.ref_load:
            self.ref_load = f"{self.base_dir.rstrip('/')}/{self.model_name}_torch_dist"

def cleanup() -> None:
    my_pid = os.getpid()
    parent_pid = os.getppid()
    exclude = f"grep -v '^{my_pid}$' | grep -v '^{parent_pid}$'"
    for process_name in ("sglang", "train.py", "MegatronTrain"):
        subprocess.run(
            f"pgrep -f '{process_name}' | {exclude} | xargs -r kill 2>/dev/null || true",
            shell=True,
            check=False,
        )
    time.sleep(5)


def prepare(args: ScriptArgs) -> None:
    backend = args.create_backend()
    backend.convert_checkpoint(
        model_name=args.model_name,
        megatron_model_type=args.megatron_model_type,
        num_gpus_per_node=args.num_gpus_per_node,
        dir_dst=args.base_dir,
        hf_checkpoint=args.hf_checkpoint,
        megatron_path=args.megatron_path,
        extra_args="--no-gradient-accumulation-fusion",
    )


def agent_train_args(args: ScriptArgs) -> str:
    external_host = ""
    if args.session_server_external_host:
        external_host = (
            f"--session-server-external-host {shlex.quote(args.session_server_external_host)} "
        )
    if args.sandbox_backend == "tencent_ags":
        agent_function = "tencent_harbor_agent.run"
    elif args.sandbox_backend == "e2b":
        agent_function = "harbor_agent_function.run"
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unsupported SANDBOX_BACKEND={args.sandbox_backend!r}; use tencent_ags or e2b"
        )
    return (
        "--custom-generate-function-path miles.rollout.generate_hub.agentic_tool_call.generate "
        f"--custom-agent-function-path {agent_function} "
        "--custom-rm-path generate.reward_func "
        "--rollout-function-path generate.RolloutFn "
        "--dynamic-sampling-filter-path "
        "miles.rollout.filter_hub.dynamic_sampling_filters.check_no_aborted "
        "--tito-model qwen3 "
        "--use-session-server v2 "
        "--session-server-port 30000 "
        f"--session-server-workers {args.session_server_workers} "
        "--session-message-matcher strict "
        f"{external_host}"
    )


def execute(args: ScriptArgs) -> None:
    backend = args.create_backend()
    checkpoint_args = (
        f"--hf-checkpoint {shlex.quote(args.hf_checkpoint)} "
        f"--ref-load {shlex.quote(args.ref_load)} "
    )
    rollout_args = (
        f"--prompt-data {shlex.quote(args.prompt_data)} "
        "--input-key prompt "
        "--metadata-key metadata "
        "--rollout-shuffle "
        f"--num-rollout {args.num_rollout} "
        f"--rollout-batch-size {args.rollout_batch_size} "
        f"--n-samples-per-prompt {args.n_samples_per_prompt} "
        "--rollout-temperature 1.0 "
        "--rollout-max-response-len 4096 "
        f"--max-seq-len {args.max_seq_len} "
        f"--global-batch-size {args.global_batch_size} "
        "--balance-data "

    performance_args = (
        "--tensor-model-parallel-size 4 "
        "--sequence-parallel "
        "--pipeline-model-parallel-size 1 "
        "--context-parallel-size 1 "
        "--expert-model-parallel-size 8 "
        "--expert-tensor-parallel-size 1 "
        "--recompute-granularity full "
        "--recompute-method uniform "
        "--recompute-num-layers 1 "
        "--no-gradient-accumulation-fusion "
        "--use-dynamic-batch-size "
        "--max-tokens-per-gpu 16384 "
        "--optimizer-cpu-offload "
        "--overlap-cpu-optimizer-d2h-h2d "
        "--use-precision-aware-optimizer "
    )
    grpo_args = (
        "--advantage-estimator grpo "
        "--use-kl-loss "
        "--kl-loss-coef 0.01 "
        "--kl-loss-type low_var_kl "
        "--entropy-coef 0.0 "
        "--eps-clip 0.2 "
        "--eps-clip-high 0.28 "
    )
    optimizer_args = (
        "--optimizer adam "
        "--lr 1e-6 "
        "--lr-decay-style constant "
        "--weight-decay 0.1 "
        "--adam-beta1 0.9 "
        "--adam-beta2 0.98 "
    )
    sglang_args = (
        "--rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 8 "
        "--sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.7 "
        "--sglang-cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 512 "
        "--sglang-tool-call-parser qwen3_coder "
        "--sglang-reasoning-parser qwen3 "
        "--sglang-router-port 31000 "
    )
    parallel_args = "--eval-global-batch-size 2 "
    misc_args = (
        "--attention-dropout 0.0 "
        "--hidden-dropout 0.0 "
        "--accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32 "
        "--attention-softmax-in-fp32 "
        "--attention-backend flash "
        "--colocate "
        f"--actor-num-nodes {args.num_nodes} "
        f"--actor-num-gpus-per-node {args.num_gpus_per_node} "
        f"--rollout-num-gpus {args.num_gpus_per_node} "
    )
    debug_args = "--debug-rollout-only " if args.mode == "debug_rollout_only" else ""
    trace_args = f"--dump-details {shlex.quote(args.save_traces_dir)} "

    train_args = "".join(
        (
            checkpoint_args,
            rollout_args,
            optimizer_args,
            grpo_args,
            trace_args,
            performance_args,
            parallel_args,
            sglang_args,
            agent_train_args(args),
            misc_args,
            debug_args,
        )
    )

    extra_env_vars = {
        "PYTHONPATH": ":".join(
            [
                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent),
                args.megatron_path,
                *agentic_pythonpath_dirs(),
                str(command_utils.repo_base_dir),
            ]
        ),
        **harbor_env_vars(args),
        "no_proxy": "127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0",
        "NO_PROXY": "127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0",
    }
    if args.miles_host_ip:
        extra_env_vars["MILES_HOST_IP"] = args.miles_host_ip
    for endpoint_var in ("E2B_API_URL", "E2B_SANDBOX_URL"):
        if os.environ.get(endpoint_var, "").strip():
            extra_env_vars[endpoint_var] = os.environ[endpoint_var]
    for runtime_var in (
        "SESSION_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL",
        "E2B_DOMAIN",
        "E2B_PROXY",
        "TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE",
        "TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REWRITE",
        "TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE",
        "TENCENT_AGS_ENVD_PORT",
        "TENCENT_AGS_FORCE_HTTP1",
        "TENCENT_AGS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT",
        "TENCENT_AGS_CREATE_RETRIES",
        "TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR",
        "TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_INSTALL_TIMEOUT",
        "TENCENT_AGS_UPLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES",
    ):
        if value := os.environ.get(runtime_var, "").strip():
            extra_env_vars[runtime_var] = value

    backend.execute_train(
        train_args=train_args,
        config=args,
        num_gpus_per_node=args.num_gpus_per_node,
        megatron_model_type=args.megatron_model_type,
        megatron_path=args.megatron_path,
        extra_env_vars=extra_env_vars,
    )


@command_utils.dataclass_cli
def main(args: ScriptArgs) -> None:
    cleanup()
    if not args.skip_prepare:
        prepare(args)
    execute(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    typer.run(main)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Aggregate Miles TITO-v2 leaf samples without assuming a fan-out cause."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import os
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DEFAULT_RESULTS = Path("/tmp/autorlbench-results")


def _as_float(value: Any) -> float | None:
    try:
        if value is None:
            return None
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _mean(values: list[float]) -> float | None:
    return sum(values) / len(values) if values else None


def _rounded(value: float | None, digits: int = 3) -> float | None:
    return round(value, digits) if value is not None else None


def load_samples(dump_dir: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    import torch

    samples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    paths = sorted(dump_dir.glob("rollout_data/*.pt"))
    for path in paths:
        payload = torch.load(path, weights_only=False, map_location="cpu")
        raw_samples = payload.get("samples", [])
        if not isinstance(raw_samples, list):
            raise AssertionError(f"{path} does not contain a sample list")
        for sample in raw_samples:
            if not isinstance(sample, dict):
                raise AssertionError(f"{path} contains a non-dict sample")
            sample = dict(sample)
            sample["dump_file"] = str(path)
            samples.append(sample)
    return samples


def build_records(samples: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    leaves: dict[int, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
    for sample in samples:
        index = sample.get("index")
        if index is None:
            raise AssertionError("a rollout sample has no sample index")
        leaves[int(index)].append(sample)

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for sample_index in sorted(leaves):
        leaf_rows = leaves[sample_index]
        metadata_rows = [row.get("metadata") or {} for row in leaf_rows]
        rewards = [value for row in leaf_rows if (value := _as_float(row.get("reward"))) is not None]
        response_lengths = [
            value
            for row in leaf_rows
            if (value := _as_float(row.get("response_length"))) is not None
        ]
        exit_statuses = [
            str(metadata.get("exit_status"))
            for metadata in metadata_rows
            if metadata.get("exit_status") is not None
        ]
        turns = [
            value
            for metadata in metadata_rows
            if (value := _as_float((metadata.get("agent_metrics") or {}).get("turns"))) is not None
        ]
        total_times = [
            value
            for metadata in metadata_rows
            if (value := _as_float((metadata.get("agent_metrics") or {}).get("total_time"))) is not None
        ]
        mismatches = [
            metadata.get("tito_session_mismatch")
            for metadata in metadata_rows
            if metadata.get("tito_session_mismatch") is not None
        ]
        trial_dirs = list(
            dict.fromkeys(
                metadata["trial_dir"]
                for metadata in metadata_rows
                if metadata.get("trial_dir")
            )
        )

        records.append(
            {
                "sample_index": sample_index,
                "group_index": leaf_rows[0].get("group_index"),
                "rollout_id": leaf_rows[0].get("rollout_id"),
                "leaf_count": len(leaf_rows),
                "statuses": [row.get("status") for row in leaf_rows],
                "exit_statuses": exit_statuses,
                "reward": _rounded(_mean(rewards)),
                "turns": _rounded(_mean(turns)),
                "response_length": _rounded(_mean(response_lengths)),
                "total_time": _rounded(_mean(total_times)),
                "tito_session_mismatch": mismatches,
                "has_tito_session_mismatch": bool(any(mismatches)),
                "trial_dirs": trial_dirs,
                "dump_files": list(
                    dict.fromkeys(
                        row["dump_file"] for row in leaf_rows if row.get("dump_file")
                    )
                ),
            }
        )
    return records


def build_summary(records: list[dict[str, Any]], samples: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    leaf_counts = [record["leaf_count"] for record in records]
    total_samples = len(samples)
    logical_rollouts = len(records)
    mismatch_records = [record for record in records if record["has_tito_session_mismatch"]]
    rewards = [record["reward"] for record in records if record["reward"] is not None]
    turns = [record["turns"] for record in records if record["turns"] is not None]
    total_times = [record["total_time"] for record in records if record["total_time"] is not None]
    exit_statuses = Counter(
        status
        for record in records
        for status in record["exit_statuses"]
    )
    statuses = Counter(
        status
        for sample in samples
        if (status := sample.get("status")) is not None
    )
    trial_dirs = {
        trial_dir
        for record in records
        for trial_dir in record["trial_dirs"]
    }

    expected_rollouts = int(os.environ.get("EXPECTED_LOGICAL_ROLLOUTS", "64"))
    return {
        "framework": "miles",
        "session_server": "v2",
        "message_matcher": "strict",
        "expected_logical_rollouts": expected_rollouts,
        "logical_rollouts": logical_rollouts,
        "training_samples": total_samples,
        "samples_per_logical_rollout": _rounded(total_samples / logical_rollouts)
        if logical_rollouts
        else None,
        "extra_training_samples": total_samples - logical_rollouts,
        "sample_inflation_ratio": _rounded(total_samples / logical_rollouts)
        if logical_rollouts
        else None,
        "fanout_rollouts": sum(count > 1 for count in leaf_counts),
        "max_leaves_per_logical_rollout": max(leaf_counts, default=0),
        "mismatch_rollouts": len(mismatch_records),
        "tito_session_mismatch_rate": _rounded(len(mismatch_records) / logical_rollouts)
        if logical_rollouts
        else None,
        "reward_mean": _rounded(_mean(rewards)),
        "positive_reward_rollouts": sum(value > 0 for value in rewards),
        "turns_mean": _rounded(_mean(turns)),
        "total_time_mean_seconds": _rounded(_mean(total_times)),
        "sample_statuses": dict(sorted(statuses.items())),
        "exit_statuses": dict(sorted(exit_statuses.items())),
        "harbor_trials": len(trial_dirs),
        "logical_rollout_count_complete": logical_rollouts == expected_rollouts,
    }


def main() -> int:
    results_dir = Path(
        os.environ.get("AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS", str(DEFAULT_RESULTS))
    )
    dump_dir = Path(

                help="Start a standalone session server for TITO/session support. "

                default=32,
                help="Number of session server instances.",
            )
            parser.add_argument(
                "--session-server-ip",
                type=str,
                default=None,
                help="Address the session servers bind to, e.g. 0.0.0.0 to accept traffic from outside "

                "Defaults to that placed address.",

            parser.add_argument(
                "--session-server-external-host",

            parser.add_argument(

"""TokenSeqComparator: segment token IDs by special-token boundaries and compare sequences."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum


@dataclass
class Segment:
    """A contiguous run of token IDs — either a special token or a content segment."""

    token_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
    is_special: bool = False


class MismatchType(Enum):
    # Segment count or structure (special/content pattern) differs between
    # expected and actual.  When this happens, segments can't be aligned so
    # no per-segment comparison is possible.
    SPECIAL_TOKEN_COUNT = "special_token_count"

    # A special-token segment has the same position in both sequences but
    # contains a different token ID.
    SPECIAL_TOKEN_TYPE = "special_token_type"

    # Non-assistant content (user, system, tool, etc.) differs.  This indicates
    # a bug in the TITO algorithm — these regions should match exactly.
    NON_ASSISTANT_TEXT = "non_assistant_text"

    # Assistant content differs.  Expected and non-severe: assistant tokens
    # are inherited directly from the pretokenized prefix across turns,
    # so they may not match the chat template's canonical tokenization.
    ASSISTANT_TEXT = "assistant_text"


@dataclass
class Mismatch:
    """A single difference found between two token sequences."""

    type: MismatchType
    segment_index: int
    expected_text: str
    actual_text: str
    detail: str = ""

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "type": self.type.value,
            "segment_index": self.segment_index,
            "expected_text": self.expected_text,
            "actual_text": self.actual_text,
            "detail": self.detail,
        }


class TokenSeqComparator:
    """Segment token sequences by special tokens and compare them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tokenizer : PreTrainedTokenizerBase
    special_token_ids : set[int] | None
        Token IDs that mark segment boundaries.  Default None auto-detects
        them (see :meth:`collect_special_ids`).  Pass an explicit set to
        override — needed when the tokenizer flags a token ``special=True``
        even though it lives inside a role's turn (e.g. Kimi's
        ``<|im_middle|>`` between role name and body) and so must not
        split the segment.
    assistant_start_str : str
        Decoded text prefix identifying assistant content segments, e.g.
        ``"<|im_start|>assistant"`` (Qwen3) or ``"<|assistant|>"`` (GLM).
        Used to classify content mismatches as assistant vs non-assistant.
    trim_trailing_ids : set[int] | None
        Token IDs to strip from both sequence tails before comparison
        (see :func:`_trim_trailing`).  Stored as a default; callers of
        :meth:`compare_sequences` may supply additional IDs that are
        **unioned** with this set.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        tokenizer,
        assistant_start_str: str,
        special_token_ids: set[int] | None = None,
        trim_trailing_ids: set[int] | None = None,
    ):
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        if special_token_ids is not None:
            self._special_ids = set(special_token_ids)
        else:
            self._special_ids = self.collect_special_ids(tokenizer)
        self._assistant_start_str = assistant_start_str
        self._trim_trailing_ids: set[int] | None = set(trim_trailing_ids) if trim_trailing_ids else None

    @staticmethod
    def collect_special_ids(tokenizer) -> set[int]:
        """Collect token IDs with ``special=True`` from the tokenizer.

        Special tokens are structural markers added by the chat template to
        delimit messages, roles, and control flow — for example
        ``<|im_start|>``, ``<|im_end|>``, ``<|endoftext|>``, ``<s>``,
        ``</s>``, and ``<|assistant|>``.

        Tokens that encode *content* produced by a role are **not** special,
        even if they look "special" to a human.  For instance, ``<think>`` and
        ``</think>`` in reasoning models are regular content tokens generated
        by the assistant — the tokenizer does not flag them as
        ``special=True``, so they are not collected here.
        """
        ids = set(tokenizer.all_special_ids)
        decoder = getattr(tokenizer, "added_tokens_decoder", None)
        if decoder:
            ids |= {k for k, v in decoder.items() if v.special}
        return ids

    def segment_by_special_tokens(self, token_ids: list[int]) -> list[Segment]:
        """Split *token_ids* into segments at special-token boundaries.

        Each special token becomes its own single-ID segment with
        ``is_special=True``.  Consecutive non-special tokens are grouped
        into content segments.  Example for Qwen3::

            [<|im_start|>, "assistant", "\\n", "Hi", <|im_end|>, "\\n"]
            → [special(<|im_start|>), content("assistant\\nHi"), special(<|im_end|>), content("\\n")]
        """
        if not token_ids:
            return []

        segments: list[Segment] = []
        current: list[int] = []
        for tid in token_ids:
            if tid in self._special_ids:
                if current:
                    segments.append(Segment(token_ids=current))
                    current = []
                segments.append(Segment(token_ids=[tid], is_special=True))
            else:
                current.append(tid)
        if current:
            segments.append(Segment(token_ids=current))
        return segments

    def compare_sequences(
        self,
        expected_ids: list[int],
        actual_ids: list[int],
        trim_trailing_ids: set[int] | None = None,
    ) -> list[Mismatch]:
        """Compare two token-ID sequences and return mismatches.

        Parameters
        ----------
        trim_trailing_ids : set[int] | None
            Additional token IDs to strip from both sequence tails before
            comparison.  **Unioned** with the IDs passed at construction time.
        """
        trim = self._trim_trailing_ids or set()
        if trim_trailing_ids:
            trim = trim | trim_trailing_ids
        if trim:
            expected_ids = _trim_trailing(expected_ids, trim)
            actual_ids = _trim_trailing(actual_ids, trim)

        exp_segs = self.segment_by_special_tokens(expected_ids)
        act_segs = self.segment_by_special_tokens(actual_ids)

        structural = self._check_segment_structure(exp_segs, act_segs)
        if structural:
            return [structural]

        mismatches: list[Mismatch] = []
        for idx, (exp, act) in enumerate(zip(exp_segs, act_segs, strict=True)):
            is_assistant_content = self._is_assistant_content(exp_segs, idx) and self._is_assistant_content(
                act_segs, idx
            )
            m = self._compare_single_segment(idx, exp, act, is_assistant_content=is_assistant_content)
            if m is not None:
                mismatches.append(m)
        return mismatches

    def _check_segment_structure(
        self,
        exp_segs: list[Segment],
        act_segs: list[Segment],
    ) -> Mismatch | None:
        """Pre-check that expected and actual segment lists have the same count
        and the same special/content pattern before per-segment comparison."""
        if len(exp_segs) != len(act_segs):
            detail = f"segment count differs: expected {len(exp_segs)}, got {len(act_segs)}"
        elif [s.is_special for s in exp_segs] != [s.is_special for s in act_segs]:
            detail = "segment structure (special/content pattern) differs"
        else:
            return None
        return Mismatch(
            type=MismatchType.SPECIAL_TOKEN_COUNT,
            segment_index=-1,
            expected_text=self._describe_structure(exp_segs),
            actual_text=self._describe_structure(act_segs),
            detail=detail,

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum


@dataclass
class Segment:
    """A contiguous run of token IDs — either a special token or a content segment."""

    token_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
    is_special: bool = False


class MismatchType(Enum):
    # Segment count or structure (special/content pattern) differs between
    # expected and actual.  When this happens, segments can't be aligned so
    # no per-segment comparison is possible.
    SPECIAL_TOKEN_COUNT = "special_token_count"

    # A special-token segment has the same position in both sequences but
    # contains a different token ID.
    SPECIAL_TOKEN_TYPE = "special_token_type"

    # Non-assistant content (user, system, tool, etc.) differs.  This indicates
    # a bug in the TITO algorithm — these regions should match exactly.
    NON_ASSISTANT_TEXT = "non_assistant_text"

    # Assistant content differs.  Expected and non-severe: assistant tokens
    # are inherited directly from the pretokenized prefix across turns,
    # so they may not match the chat template's canonical tokenization.
    ASSISTANT_TEXT = "assistant_text"


@dataclass
class Mismatch:
    """A single difference found between two token sequences."""

    type: MismatchType
    segment_index: int
    expected_text: str
    actual_text: str
    detail: str = ""

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "type": self.type.value,
            "segment_index": self.segment_index,
            "expected_text": self.expected_text,
            "actual_text": self.actual_text,
            "detail": self.detail,
        }


class TokenSeqComparator:
    """Segment token sequences by special tokens and compare them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tokenizer : PreTrainedTokenizerBase
    special_token_ids : set[int] | None
        Token IDs that mark segment boundaries.  Default None auto-detects
        them (see :meth:`collect_special_ids`).  Pass an explicit set to
        override — needed when the tokenizer flags a token ``special=True``
        even though it lives inside a role's turn (e.g. Kimi's
        ``<|im_middle|>`` between role name and body) and so must not
        split the segment.
    assistant_start_str : str
        Decoded text prefix identifying assistant content segments, e.g.
        ``"<|im_start|>assistant"`` (Qwen3) or ``"<|assistant|>"`` (GLM).
        Used to classify content mismatches as assistant vs non-assistant.
    trim_trailing_ids : set[int] | None
        Token IDs to strip from both sequence tails before comparison
        (see :func:`_trim_trailing`).  Stored as a default; callers of
        :meth:`compare_sequences` may supply additional IDs that are
        **unioned** with this set.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        tokenizer,
        assistant_start_str: str,
        special_token_ids: set[int] | None = None,
        trim_trailing_ids: set[int] | None = None,
    ):
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        if special_token_ids is not None:
            self._special_ids = set(special_token_ids)
        else:
            self._special_ids = self.collect_special_ids(tokenizer)
        self._assistant_start_str = assistant_start_str
        self._trim_trailing_ids: set[int] | None = set(trim_trailing_ids) if trim_trailing_ids else None

    @staticmethod
    def collect_special_ids(tokenizer) -> set[int]:
        """Collect token IDs with ``special=True`` from the tokenizer.

        Special tokens are structural markers added by the chat template to
        delimit messages, roles, and control flow — for example
        ``<|im_start|>``, ``<|im_end|>``, ``<|endoftext|>``, ``<s>``,
        ``</s>``, and ``<|assistant|>``.

        Tokens that encode *content* produced by a role are **not** special,
        even if they look "special" to a human.  For instance, ``<think>`` and
        ``</think>`` in reasoning models are regular content tokens generated
        by the assistant — the tokenizer does not flag them as
        ``special=True``, so they are not collected here.
        """
        ids = set(tokenizer.all_special_ids)
        decoder = getattr(tokenizer, "added_tokens_decoder", None)
        if decoder:
            ids |= {k for k, v in decoder.items() if v.special}
        return ids

    def segment_by_special_tokens(self, token_ids: list[int]) -> list[Segment]:
        """Split *token_ids* into segments at special-token boundaries.

        Each special token becomes its own single-ID segment with
        ``is_special=True``.  Consecutive non-special tokens are grouped
        into content segments.  Example for Qwen3::

            [<|im_start|>, "assistant", "\\n", "Hi", <|im_end|>, "\\n"]
            → [special(<|im_start|>), content("assistant\\nHi"), special(<|im_end|>), content("\\n")]
        """
        if not token_ids:
            return []

        segments: list[Segment] = []
        current: list[int] = []
        for tid in token_ids:
            if tid in self._special_ids:
                if current:
                    segments.append(Segment(token_ids=current))
                    current = []
                segments.append(Segment(token_ids=[tid], is_special=True))
            else:
                current.append(tid)
        if current:
            segments.append(Segment(token_ids=current))
        return segments

    def compare_sequences(
        self,
        expected_ids: list[int],
        actual_ids: list[int],
        trim_trailing_ids: set[int] | None = None,
    ) -> list[Mismatch]:
        """Compare two token-ID sequences and return mismatches.

        Parameters
        ----------
        trim_trailing_ids : set[int] | None
            Additional token IDs to strip from both sequence tails before
            comparison.  **Unioned** with the IDs passed at construction time.
        """
        trim = self._trim_trailing_ids or set()
        if trim_trailing_ids:
            trim = trim | trim_trailing_ids
        if trim:
            expected_ids = _trim_trailing(expected_ids, trim)
            actual_ids = _trim_trailing(actual_ids, trim)

        exp_segs = self.segment_by_special_tokens(expected_ids)
        act_segs = self.segment_by_special_tokens(actual_ids)

        structural = self._check_segment_structure(exp_segs, act_segs)
        if structural:
            return [structural]

        mismatches: list[Mismatch] = []
        for idx, (exp, act) in enumerate(zip(exp_segs, act_segs, strict=True)):
            is_assistant_content = self._is_assistant_content(exp_segs, idx) and self._is_assistant_content(
                act_segs, idx
            )
            m = self._compare_single_segment(idx, exp, act, is_assistant_content=is_assistant_content)
            if m is not None:
                mismatches.append(m)
        return mismatches

    def _check_segment_structure(
        self,
        exp_segs: list[Segment],
        act_segs: list[Segment],
    ) -> Mismatch | None:
        """Pre-check that expected and actual segment lists have the same count
        and the same special/content pattern before per-segment comparison."""
        if len(exp_segs) != len(act_segs):
            detail = f"segment count differs: expected {len(exp_segs)}, got {len(act_segs)}"
        elif [s.is_special for s in exp_segs] != [s.is_special for s in act_segs]:
            detail = "segment structure (special/content pattern) differs"
        else:
            return None
        return Mismatch(
            type=MismatchType.SPECIAL_TOKEN_COUNT,
            segment_index=-1,
            expected_text=self._describe_structure(exp_segs),
            actual_text=self._describe_structure(act_segs),
            detail=detail,

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# sglang parser resolution (per-family binding + assert-equal on user input)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def resolve_reasoning_and_tool_call_parser(
    tito_model: TITOTokenizerType | str,
    user_reasoning_parser: str | None = None,
    user_tool_call_parser: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Resolve sglang ``--reasoning-parser`` and ``--tool-call-parser`` for the
    given TITO family.

    Both parsers are bound on the TITO subclass as class attributes because
    the model's reasoning / tool-call emission shapes are per-family facts.
    For each parser independently:

    * If the user didn't pass a value, return the family's bound value
      (which may itself be ``None`` for ``DEFAULT`` or unbound subclasses
      — the caller is then responsible for supplying one downstream).
    * If the user passed a value and the family is bound, assert equality;
      a mismatch is a configuration bug and raises ``ValueError`` rather
      than silently overriding.
    * If the user passed a value and the family is unbound, accept it.

    Returns ``(reasoning_parser, tool_call_parser)``.
    """
    if isinstance(tito_model, str):
        tito_model = TITOTokenizerType(tito_model)
    cls = TITOTokenizerType.get_tokenizer_class(tito_model)

    def _resolve_one(field: str, bound: str | None, user: str | None) -> str | None:
        if user is None:
            return bound
        if bound is None:
            return user
        if user != bound:
            raise ValueError(
                f"--{field.replace('_', '-')}={user!r} disagrees with the parser "
                f"registered for tito_model={tito_model.value!r}: {bound!r}. The "
                f"parser is bound on the TITO subclass; either pass {bound!r} or "
                f"omit the flag to auto-resolve."
            )
        return user

    return (
        _resolve_one("reasoning_parser", cls.reasoning_parser, user_reasoning_parser),
        _resolve_one("tool_call_parser", cls.tool_call_parser, user_tool_call_parser),
    )

import logging
from argparse import Namespace
from typing import Any

from miles.rollout.generate_utils.sample_utils import merge_samples
from miles.rollout.session.errors import TokenizationError
from miles.rollout.session.request_args import filter_turn_args
from miles.rollout.session.samples.merge import (
    compute_samples_from_openai_records,
    merge_samples_with_addition_r3,
    truncate_samples_by_total_tokens,
)
from miles.rollout.session.v2.session_state import SessionRegistryV2, SessionStateV2
from miles.utils.types import Sample

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def tree_metadata(state: SessionStateV2) -> dict:
    """The structural layer: node and leaf tables, index-aligned with commits.

    ``response_id`` is the branch<->leaf join key — the agent saw the same id
    in each chat response, so the semantic layer can key per-branch data on it.
    """
    nodes = [
        {
            "id": node.seq,
            "parent": node.parent.seq if node.parent is not None else None,
            "seq": node.seq,
            "truncated": node.truncated,
            "committed_at": node.committed_at,
            "completion_span": list(node.completion_span),
            "num_tokens": len(node.token_ids),
            "response_id": node.response_id,
            "turn_args": filter_turn_args(node.turn_args),
        }
        for node in state.tree.nodes
    ]
    leaves = [
        {"node_id": leaf.seq, "path_node_ids": [n.seq for n in leaf.path_nodes()]} for leaf in state.tree.leaves()
    ]
    return {"nodes": nodes, "leaves": leaves}


def build_leaf_material(
    args: Namespace,
    state: SessionStateV2,
    registry: SessionRegistryV2,
    *,
    session_id: str,
    max_seq_len: int | None,
    use_addition_r3: bool = False,
) -> list[Sample]:
    """Merge each leaf's root-to-leaf node records into one raw sample, in commit order.

    Leaves whose turns all truncate away are dropped. Each sample's metadata
    carries the ``leaf`` descriptor plus the flat TITO bookkeeping keys for
    the downstream pick/post-process hooks (the per-leaf counterpart of the
    session metadata a v1 sample receives whole).

    With ``use_addition_r3``, each record along a path carries only its
    additional R3 rows; the per-leaf assembler materializes the required prefix
    because a path is the linear record chain its offsets were computed on.
    """
    material: list[Sample] = []
    for leaf in state.tree.leaves():
        path = leaf.path_nodes()
        records = [node.record for node in path]
        turns = compute_samples_from_openai_records(
            args,
            records,
            registry.tokenizer,
            accumulated_token_ids=leaf.token_ids,
            max_trim_tokens=registry.tito_tokenizer.max_trim_tokens,
            use_addition_r3=use_addition_r3,

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class SessionCoreV2(SessionCore):
    """``SessionCore`` with tree serving: overrides the session-semantics
    methods (positioning/commit, metadata, samples op), inherits the
    transport shell (health, create/delete, raw proxy)."""

    def __init__(
        self, backend, registry: SessionRegistryV2, config, session_server_instance_id=None, *, use_addition_r3=False
    ):
        super().__init__(backend, registry, config, session_server_instance_id, use_addition_r3=use_addition_r3)
        # Import-path only in production: function_registry is process-local.
        self.sample_picker = load_function(config.session_sample_picker_path, sync_required=True)
        self.sample_postprocessor = load_function(config.session_sample_postprocessor_path, sync_required=True)

    def _session_metadata(self, session_id: str, session) -> dict:
        """Mirrors ``core.SessionCore._session_metadata``: token ids come from
        the latest committed generation's path, plus the ``tree`` block."""
        metadata: dict = {}
        try:
            mismatch = self.registry.compute_session_mismatch(session)
        except TokenizationError:
            logger.exception("Failed to compute tito_session_mismatch for session %s", session_id)
            mismatch = None
        if mismatch is not None:
            metadata["tito_session_mismatch"] = mismatch
        latest = session.latest()
        metadata["accumulated_token_ids"] = latest.token_ids if latest is not None else []
        metadata["max_trim_tokens"] = self.registry.tito_tokenizer.max_trim_tokens
        metadata["tree"] = tree_metadata(session)
        metadata["turn_args"] = filter_turn_args(latest.turn_args) if latest is not None else {}
        return metadata

    async def get_session(self, session_id: str) -> Response:
        """Mirrors ``core.SessionCore.get_session``, serving the records along the
        latest committed generation's path."""
        session = self.registry.get_session(session_id)
        metadata = self._session_metadata(session_id, session)
        latest = session.latest()
        records = [node.record for node in latest.path_nodes()] if latest is not None else []
        payload = GetSessionResponse(session_id=session_id, records=records, metadata=metadata)
        return Response(
            content=_render_json(payload.model_dump(mode="json")), status_code=200, media_type=JSON_MEDIA_TYPE
        )

    async def collect_samples(
        self, session_id: str, *, max_seq_len: int | None, agent_metadata: dict | None = None
    ) -> Response:
        """Samples op: assemble one raw sample per leaf, then run the
        pick/post-process hook pipeline and encode the result.

        Synchronous on the server loop (no await), so the session read cannot
        interleave with chat commits. Deterministic assembly/hook failures map
        to 422; unknown exceptions propagate.
        """
        session = self.registry.get_session(session_id)
        metadata = self._session_metadata(session_id, session)
        fields = COMPUTED_FIELDS_V2
        if session.sampling_support_replay:
            fields += ROLLOUT_SAMPLING_MASK_FIELDS

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Route the public Harbor agent function to the Tencent AGS environment."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import base64
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import harbor_agent_function
import harbor.agents.installed.mini_swe_agent as mini_swe_agent
from harbor.agents.installed.mini_swe_agent import MiniSweAgent


_original_environment_config = harbor_agent_function._environment_config
_INSTALL_TIMEOUT = int(os.getenv("TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_INSTALL_TIMEOUT", "1800"))
_UPLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES = int(os.getenv("TENCENT_AGS_UPLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES", str(32 * 1024 * 1024)))


async def _install_mini_swe_agent(self: MiniSweAgent, environment: Any) -> None:
    wheelhouse_tar = Path(os.environ["TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR"]).expanduser()
    if not wheelhouse_tar.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            "set TENCENT_AGS_AGENT_WHEELHOUSE_TAR to a Python 3.10 wheelhouse tar.gz"
        )

    sandbox = environment._sandbox
    with wheelhouse_tar.open("rb") as wheelhouse_file:
        part_index = 0
        while chunk := wheelhouse_file.read(_UPLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES):
            await sandbox.files.write(
                f"/tmp/agent-wheelhouse.tar.gz.part-{part_index:04d}",
                chunk,
                user="root",
                request_timeout=_INSTALL_TIMEOUT,
                use_octet_stream=True,
            )
            part_index += 1

    version_spec = f"=={self._version}" if self._version else ""
    output_cap_b64 = base64.b64encode(
        mini_swe_agent._OUTPUT_CAP_PATCH.format(
            cap_bytes=mini_swe_agent.MAX_COMMAND_OUTPUT_BYTES
        ).encode()
    ).decode()
    step_timing_b64 = base64.b64encode(
        mini_swe_agent._STEP_TIMING_PATCH.encode()
    ).decode()
    await self.exec_as_root(
        environment,
        command=(
            "set -euo pipefail; "
            "cat /tmp/agent-wheelhouse.tar.gz.part-* > /tmp/agent-wheelhouse.tar.gz; "
            "tar -xzf /tmp/agent-wheelhouse.tar.gz -C /tmp; "
            "/usr/bin/python3.10 -m pip install --no-index "
            "--find-links /tmp/agent-wheelhouse uv==0.7.13; "
            "export UV_OFFLINE=1; "
            'export PATH="/usr/local/bin:/root/.local/bin:$PATH"; '
            f"uv tool install mini-swe-agent{version_spec} "
            "--with 'litellm[proxy]' "
            "--find-links /tmp/agent-wheelhouse "
            "--python /usr/bin/python3.10; "
            'agent_python="$(uv tool dir)/mini-swe-agent/bin/python"; '
            f'echo {output_cap_b64} | base64 -d | "$agent_python" - && '
            f'echo {step_timing_b64} | base64 -d | "$agent_python" - && '
            "mini-swe-agent --help && "
            "/usr/bin/python3.10 -m pip install --no-index "
            "--find-links /tmp/agent-wheelhouse "
            "swebench==4.0.3 datasets==2.16.1 'fastcore<1.11'"
        ),
        env={"UV_OFFLINE": "1"},
        timeout_sec=_INSTALL_TIMEOUT,
    )


MiniSweAgent.install = _install_mini_swe_agent


def _environment_config():
    config = _original_environment_config()
    template = os.getenv("TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE", "").strip()
    if template:
        config.kwargs.setdefault("prebuilt_template_id", template)
    config.import_path = "tencent_ags_e2b:E2BEnvironment"
    return config


harbor_agent_function._environment_config = _environment_config


async def run(
    base_url: str,
    prompt: Any,
    request_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    public_session_url = os.getenv("SESSION_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL", "").strip().rstrip("/")
    if public_session_url:
        base_url = re.sub(r"^https?://[^/]+", public_session_url, base_url)
    return await harbor_agent_function.run(
        base_url,
        prompt,
        request_kwargs=request_kwargs,
        metadata=metadata,
        **kwargs,
    )

node the request continues; the request args against that node's ``turn_args``;

node. What ``GET /sessions`` shows as a single chain is

derived, never stored.

"""Session state over the trajectory tree: always-branch serving.

This module is the serving policy on top. A request is never rejected for mismatching stored history and never
destroys anything: it attaches at the deepest matching node, its unmatched
suffix becomes the new branch's delta, and whatever is not a clean
extension just grows a sibling or a new root. Whether a branch was a retry
is decided later by the sample_picker, not here.

Concurrency contract: single lock on the whole tree. A commit only appends a new
node under the parent the request attached to, so concurrent generations from
the same spot become sibling nodes instead of a conflict.

The tree is the whole state. Serving a request is
``prepare_token_ids_and_request_args`` (``attach_point_for_request``, pure: which
node the request continues; the request args against that node's ``turn_args``;
the prompt rendered under that node) and then ``commit_generation`` under that
node. What ``GET /sessions`` shows as a single chain is
``SessionStateV2.latest()``, the most recently committed generation's path —
derived, never stored.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from miles.rollout.session.config import SessionServerConfig
from miles.rollout.session.errors import MessageValidationError, TokenizationError, TruncatedGenerationError
from miles.rollout.session.linear_trajectory import SessionRegistry, assert_pretokenized_prefix
from miles.rollout.session.request_args import PreparedChatRequest, prepare_chat_request
from miles.rollout.session.types import SessionRecord
from miles.rollout.session.v2.tree_trajectory import AttachPoint, SessionTree, TrajectoryNode
from miles.utils.chat_template_utils.message_matcher_hub import SessionMessageMatcher
from miles.utils.chat_template_utils.tito_tokenizer import TITOTokenizer, extract_template_args

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class SessionStateV2:
    """Per-session concurrency container plus the trajectory forest.

    The forest is the whole state; ``latest()`` derives the single chain that
    ``GET /sessions`` serves. A failed first turn commits nothing, so the
    session stays fully retryable.
    """

    lock: asyncio.Lock = field(default_factory=asyncio.Lock, repr=False, compare=False)
    closing: bool = field(default=False, repr=False, compare=False)
    tree: SessionTree = field(default_factory=SessionTree)
    evaluation: bool = False
    sampling_defaults: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    sampling_support_replay: bool = False

    def latest(self) -> TrajectoryNode | None:
        """The most recently committed generation (always a leaf), or ``None``
        before the first commit. Its root->node path is the single-chain view."""
        return self.tree.nodes[-1] if self.tree.nodes else None


def attach_point_for_request(
    state: SessionStateV2,
    request_messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    message_matcher: SessionMessageMatcher | None = None,
) -> AttachPoint:
    """Where *request_messages* attaches: the deepest node whose path is a
    prefix of the request, ``node=None`` for a new root. Pure; raises 409 when
    that node is a truncated generation."""
    attach = state.tree.find_attach_point(request_messages, message_matcher=message_matcher)

    if attach.node is not None and attach.node.truncated:
        raise TruncatedGenerationError(
            "truncated generation cannot be extended: the matched node ended with "
            "finish_reason='length' and truncation closes that path for good; "
            "branch before the cut instead"
        )

        logger.debug(
            "Branching: request(%d msgs) attaches at node seq=%s "
            "(matched %d msgs, best overlap %d), tree has %d nodes",
            len(request_messages),
            attach.node.seq if attach.node is not None else "<new root>",
            attach.matched_messages,
            attach.best_overlap,
            len(state.tree.nodes),
        )
    return attach

    message_matcher: SessionMessageMatcher | None = None,

steps.reasoning_content:
Now, is `qwen3_coder` actually the wrong parser for Qwen3-30B-A3B? Let's verify from sglang knowledge. SGLang tool call parsers:
- `qwen25`: parses `<tool_call>\n{"name": ..., "arguments": ...}\n</tool_call>` (Hermes-style JSON). Used for Qwen2.5 and Qwen3.
- `qwen3_coder`: parses `<tool_call>\n<function=name>\n<parameter=key>\nvalue\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>`.

Yes, Qwen3-Coder's format is XML. The Qwen3-30B-A3B (non-coder) emits JSON. The actual_text confirms JSON format. With `qwen3_coder`, parser finds no tool call → agent sees none.

Also, the TITO family `qwen3` binds `tool_call_parser = "qwen25"`, and the `resolve_reasoning_and_tool_call_parser` docstring says a mismatch is a configuration bug and raises ValueError — but it's only called in the test harness (`session_verify_runner`), not in the training launch path. Let me verify that claim: grep for where args.sglang_tool_call_parser is reconciled. Only session_verify_runner calls resolve. So yes.

Now what about the "unproven" separate MiniSWE behavior: 3 leaves per logical rollout (fanout), 192 training samples. Is that caused by the parser defect (MiniSWE retries 3 format errors → 3 assistant generations, each branching)? Or is it inherent MiniSWE retry behavior? The task says "Distinguish the configuration defect from any separate residual MiniSWE behavior; do not merge them into one unproven root cause."

Interpretation: The config defect (wrong tool-call parser) causes the session mismatches. The MiniSWE behavior (max_consecutive_format_errors=3; on "No tool calls found" it re-prompts) is a separate behavior — it isn't itself the root cause of mismatch, but it's what turns each parser failure into 3 separate "logical-rollout-like" leaf samples: mini-swe-agent executes 3 turns per failed trial → 3 leaves in v2 tree → 192 training samples instead of 64.

Hmm, but is the 3 leaves really because of 3 assistant generations? Let's test: 3 leaves per record with segment indices 9,13,17, differing by 4. If the tree were linear, only the deepest leaf remains; the fact that all 3 assistant segments are leaves at different depths means the tree branched at the same attach point? Let's think again about the segment counts.

Suppose messages: [system(2 segs), user(2), assistant1]. Segments: special system, content, special end; special user, content, special end; special assistant, content = ... Let's count for Qwen3: each message = <|im_start|> (1 special), content (1 content), <|im_end|> (1 special), newline (1 content). So system = seg0 special, seg1 content("system\n..."), seg2 special, seg3 content("\n"). user = seg4 special, seg5 content("user\n..."), seg6 special, seg7 content("\n"). assistant1 = seg8 special, seg9 content("assistant\n<think>..."), seg10 special, seg11 content("\n"). user_error = seg12 special, seg13 content("user\nTool call error..."), ...

Ah, so segment_index 9 = assistant1 content; 13 = user error1 content (!), and 17 = ... hmm. Wait 13 would be assistant2? Let's count: after assistant1: special8, content9, special10 (im_end), content11 ("\n"). Then user_error: special12, content13, special14, content15. Then assistant2: special16, content17.

Hmm, but all mismatches are type assistant_text and text begins with "assistant\n<think>". Segment 13 text begins with "assistant\n<think>..." in record 0 leaf1. So segment 13 is an assistant content segment, not user. So my segment count is off (maybe system/user messages don't produce separate newline content segments, or segment indices count differently because tabby). Let's not infer exact structure.

Anyway, 3 leaves each with one assistant_text mismatch at different segment indices suggests three separate trajectories of different lengths are leaves: perhaps because the three assistant turns are siblings.

Actually here's a cleaner hypothesis: mini-swe-agent does **not** send the assistant's prior tool-call-less message back? Let's examine mini-swe-agent 2.x behavior: In `DefaultAgent.step`, it does:
```
message = self.model.query(self.messages)
self.messages.append(message)
...
output = self.env.execute(action)
self.messages.append({"role":"user","content": observation})
```
On no tool calls, it appends the assistant message and a user "Tool call error" message. So history grows linearly.

But the *session server* attaches requests based on `find_attach_point` with strict matcher. The client replays the assistant message. The stored assistant message (server-side) has content="" and reasoning_content=<think>. The client's replayed assistant message from litellm has content="" too (as returned). Should match. But reasoning_content may not be echoed by litellm? If the client sends the assistant message without `reasoning_content`, strict matching fails. Then the request attaches at the previous user node, and delta includes the replayed assistant message + error user + new assistant. That yields a sibling branch each turn → 3 leaves, exactly.

Wait, but then the mismatch expected for leaf0 segment 17 would be computed on path messages that include replayed assistant messages (without reasoning_content) which the template renders as content-only (no think markers) → expected would differ earlier than the ending. Hmm, but expected does start with "assistant\n<think>"...

OK. Let me stop over-modeling the tree and focus on what's provable from the artifacts:

Facts:
- 64 logical rollouts (all 64 expected), 64 harbor trials, 64 sessions.
- Each logical rollout produced 3 leaves (leaf_count 3 for all 64); max_leaves_per_logical_rollout=3; fanout_rollouts=64; 192 training samples; sample_inflation_ratio 3.0; extra_training_samples 128.
- All 187 ATOMIC mismatches are type `assistant_text`; session-level tito_session_mismatch_rate/v2 = 0.973958 (i.e., 187/192 samples), rollout-level mismatch_rollouts=64/64 → rate 1.0.
- All mismatch diffs are exactly: canonical render ends after `</think>\n\n`; actual accumulated token text continues with `<tool_call>\n{"name": ..., "arguments": ...}\n</tool_call>`.
- All 64 trials have exactly 2 ATIF steps and exit with RepeatedFormatError (or "Submitted" statuses?) — mini-swe-agent reports "No tool calls found in the response" 3 times → RepeatedFormatError. Let me verify this pattern across all trials: mini-swe-agent.txt tails. Also check which are "Submitted" vs "AgentError" — maybe Submitted means the agent submitted? But all rewards 0.

# Selected SWE-bench Verified data

`prepare_data.py` selects 16 complete records from the
`princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified` test split. Selection is deterministic:
group records by repository in dataset order, then choose one record from each
repository in round-robin order until 16 records are selected.

The selection excludes instance IDs documented by the public Harbor SWE-bench
adapter as known environment or verifier outliers.

Generated files:

- `swebench_verified.jsonl`: complete dataset records used to build Harbor tasks.
- `miles_prompts.jsonl`: Miles prompt rows with `instance_id` and
  `agent_name=mini-swe-agent`.
- `selected_instance_ids.txt`: the 16 instance IDs, in selection order.

The RL run samples each of the 16 prompts four times, producing 64 logical
rollouts for one GRPO update.

Consider the following model:

```python
from astropy.modeling import models as m
from astropy.modeling.separable import separability_matrix

cm = m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5)
```

It's separability matrix as you might expect is a diagonal:

```python
>>> separability_matrix(cm)
array([[ True, False],
       [False,  True]])
```

If I make the model more complex:
```python
>>> separability_matrix(m.Pix2Sky_TAN() & m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5))
array([[ True,  True, False, False],
       [ True,  True, False, False],
       [False, False,  True, False],
       [False, False, False,  True]])
```

The output matrix is again, as expected, the outputs and inputs to the linear models are separable and independent of each other.

If however, I nest these compound models:
```python
>>> separability_matrix(m.Pix2Sky_TAN() & cm)
array([[ True,  True, False, False],
       [ True,  True, False, False],
       [False, False,  True,  True],
       [False, False,  True,  True]])
```
Suddenly the inputs and outputs are no longer separable?

This feels like a bug to me, but I might be missing something?
"}

def run_session_verify(args: argparse.Namespace, *, wire_format: SessionWireFormat = "openai") -> None:
    """Boot ``miles`` rollout pipeline and run the session-verification driver.

    Returns nothing on success; raises ``AssertionError`` on TITO mismatch
    (HTTP 500 from server-side prefix check) or coverage shortfall raised by the selected generate wrapper.

    ``args`` MUST be a fully-shaped Namespace carrying miles-canonical field
    names plus the session-verify-specific fields (``session_verify_cycles``,
    ``tool_call_failure_mode``, ``assistant_text_threshold``).  Build it via
    ``parse_args(add_custom_arguments=session_verify_extras)`` for the CLI
    path or by spreading ``SESSION_VERIFY_INVARIANT_ARGS`` into
    ``argparse.Namespace(...)`` for tests.

    Mutates ``args`` in two places before composing train_args:
    - ``args.sglang_reasoning_parser`` / ``args.sglang_tool_call_parser`` are
      resolved against the TITO subclass's bound values via
      ``resolve_reasoning_and_tool_call_parser`` — caller-passed values that
      disagree with the bound values raise ``ValueError`` here, before any
      GPU work starts.
    - ``args.hf_checkpoint`` is replaced with the local download path so the
      composed train_args points at the downloaded model, not the HF id.
    """
    if wire_format not in ("openai", "anthropic"):
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported session verification wire format: {wire_format}")

    backend = command_utils.default_config().create_backend()
    args.sglang_reasoning_parser, args.sglang_tool_call_parser = resolve_reasoning_and_tool_call_parser(
        args.tito_model, args.sglang_reasoning_parser, args.sglang_tool_call_parser
    )
    _ensure_prompt_data()
    _clear_proxy_env()
    args.hf_checkpoint = _ensure_model_downloaded(args.hf_checkpoint, backend=backend)

    train_args = namespace_to_train_args(args)

    # Per-sample token-seq metrics file: rollout workers append one JSONL line
    # per sample inside the selected generate wrapper; we aggregate after
    # execute_train returns to apply the assistant_text soft threshold.
    metrics_fd, metrics_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="session_verify_metrics_", suffix=".jsonl")
    os.close(metrics_fd)

    try:
        backend.execute_train(
            train_args=train_args,
            num_gpus_per_node=args.actor_num_gpus_per_node,
            megatron_model_type=None,
            extra_env_vars=_session_verify_env(args, metrics_path, wire_format=wire_format),
        )
        assert_session_verify_metrics(
            metrics_path,
            assistant_text_threshold=args.assistant_text_threshold,
            special_token_count_threshold=getattr(args, "ci_tito_special_token_count_threshold", 0.0),
            require_append_tool=wire_format == "openai",
        )
    except Exception:
        preserved_metrics_path = metrics_path + ".failed"
        try:
            shutil.copy(metrics_path, preserved_metrics_path)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Failed to preserve per-sample mismatch payloads at %s", preserved_metrics_path)
        else:
            logger.error("Preserved per-sample mismatch payloads at %s for post-mortem", preserved_metrics_path)
        raise
    finally:
        try:
            os.unlink(metrics_path)
        except OSError:
            pass

def run_session_verify(args: argparse.Namespace, *, wire_format: SessionWireFormat = "openai") -> None:
    """Boot ``miles`` rollout pipeline and run the session-verification driver.

    Returns nothing on success; raises ``AssertionError`` on TITO mismatch
    (HTTP 500 from server-side prefix check) or coverage shortfall raised by the selected generate wrapper.

    ``args`` MUST be a fully-shaped Namespace carrying miles-canonical field
    names plus the session-verify-specific fields (``session_verify_cycles``,
    ``tool_call_failure_mode``, ``assistant_text_threshold``).  Build it via
    ``parse_args(add_custom_arguments=session_verify_extras)`` for the CLI
    path or by spreading ``SESSION_VERIFY_INVARIANT_ARGS`` into
    ``argparse.Namespace(...)`` for tests.

    Mutates ``args`` in two places before composing train_args:
    - ``args.sglang_reasoning_parser`` / ``args.sglang_tool_call_parser`` are
      resolved against the TITO subclass's bound values via
      ``resolve_reasoning_and_tool_call_parser`` — caller-passed values that
      disagree with the bound values raise ``ValueError`` here, before any
      GPU work starts.
    - ``args.hf_checkpoint`` is replaced with the local download path so the
      composed train_args points at the downloaded model, not the HF id.
    """
    if wire_format not in ("openai", "anthropic"):
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported session verification wire format: {wire_format}")

    backend = command_utils.default_config().create_backend()
    args.sglang_reasoning_parser, args.sglang_tool_call_parser = resolve_reasoning_and_tool_call_parser(
        args.tito_model, args.sglang_reasoning_parser, args.sglang_tool_call_parser
    )
    _ensure_prompt_data()
    _clear_proxy_env()
    args.hf_checkpoint = _ensure_model_downloaded(args.hf_checkpoint, backend=backend)

    train_args = namespace_to_train_args(args)

    # Per-sample token-seq metrics file: rollout workers append one JSONL line
    # per sample inside the selected generate wrapper; we aggregate after
    # execute_train returns to apply the assistant_text soft threshold.
    metrics_fd, metrics_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="session_verify_metrics_", suffix=".jsonl")
    os.close(metrics_fd)

    try:
        backend.execute_train(
            train_args=train_args,
            num_gpus_per_node=args.actor_num_gpus_per_node,
            megatron_model_type=None,
            extra_env_vars=_session_verify_env(args, metrics_path, wire_format=wire_format),
        )
        assert_session_verify_metrics(
            metrics_path,
            assistant_text_threshold=args.assistant_text_threshold,
            special_token_count_threshold=getattr(args, "ci_tito_special_token_count_threshold", 0.0),
            require_append_tool=wire_format == "openai",
        )
    except Exception:
        preserved_metrics_path = metrics_path + ".failed"
        try:
            shutil.copy(metrics_path, preserved_metrics_path)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Failed to preserve per-sample mismatch payloads at %s", preserved_metrics_path)
        else:
            logger.error("Preserved per-sample mismatch payloads at %s for post-mortem", preserved_metrics_path)
        raise
    finally:
        try:
            os.unlink(metrics_path)
        except OSError:

steps.reasoning_content:
The log prints the *messages sent* to the model. Each turn it prints "System:", "User:" (task), then "User: Tool call error...". There's no Assistant block. In mini-swe-agent's log format, when printing the messages before a query, it typically prints all messages with role labels. Since there's no "Assistant:" anywhere, MiniSWE's format-error handling appears to NOT append the assistant message (or it replaces the last message). Actually in mini-swe-agent 2.x, `DefaultAgent._query()` prints the messages; the `handle_format_error` likely does:
```
self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Tool call error..."})
```
but the assistant message appended by `self.messages.append(message)` may be an assistant message with empty content — would still print "Assistant:" if it prints all. Hmm, maybe their log only prints messages with non-empty content! An assistant message with content="" and no tool calls might be skipped by the formatter. That's plausible.

Either way, the key provable claim: each retry request does not extend the stored path (the stored assistant node from the previous attempt is not part of the next request), so under v2 always-branch each attempt becomes a new root/leaf. We can state this as observed behavior and attribute it to MiniSWE's format-error retry loop, without over-claiming the exact field-level reason.

Hmm, but I want a defensible causal chain. Let me check `find_attach_point` more: request2 = [system, user, user_error]. Node0 delta=[system,user,assistant1]. Matching: delta[0] system vs system ok; delta[1] user vs user ok; delta[2] assistant1 vs request[2]=user_error → mismatch at i=2 < 3 → partial delta → node0 not candidate → best None → new root. Yes → new root. So request2 creates a new root, containing delta = [system, user, user_error, assistant2]. Request3 = [system,user,user_error1,user_error2]: node0 partial at 2; root1 delta [system,user,user_error1,assistant2] matches first 3, diverges at assistant2 vs user_error2 → partial → new root. So 3 roots. Exactly 3 leaves, exactly 3 assistant generations. Yes, this is provable from the structure (given the client doesn't replay assistant messages).

But is it plausible that mini-swe-agent doesn't replay assistant messages on a format error? Let me check mini-swe-agent's source in the sandbox? We have the wheelhouse tar path but not the file. Maybe pip has mini-swe-agent installed? Check dist-packages. We saw litellm and harbor installed here. Maybe mini-swe-agent too.

def _extract_subtiming_msec(
    mini_swe_agent_trajectory: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
    """Collect the per-step LLM-wait and tool-exec durations (in msec) that the
    install-time timing patch stamps onto each message's ``extra``.

    Returns the two lists under the same keys terminus-2 uses
    (``api_request_times_msec`` / ``command_exec_times_msec``) so the dashboard's
    sub-timing logic surfaces them unchanged. Empty lists are omitted, so a run
    produced without the timing patch yields ``{}`` and the dashboard simply
    drops the two sub-rows.
    """
    llm_wait: list[float] = []
    tool_exec: list[float] = []
    for message in mini_swe_agent_trajectory.get("messages") or []:
        extra = message.get("extra") or {}
        wait = extra.get("harbor_llm_wait_msec")
        if isinstance(wait, (int, float)):
            llm_wait.append(float(wait))
        exec_ = extra.get("harbor_tool_exec_msec")
        if isinstance(exec_, (int, float)):
            tool_exec.append(float(exec_))
    out: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    if llm_wait:
        out["api_request_times_msec"] = llm_wait
    if tool_exec:
        out["command_exec_times_msec"] = tool_exec
    return out


def _parse_response_output(
    message: dict[str, Any], step_id: int
) -> tuple[str, str | None, list[ToolCall] | None]:
    """Responses-API analogue of ``_parse_tool_calls``: a ``LitellmResponseModel``
    turn is the raw response object (no ``role``) with text/reasoning/tool calls in
    ``output``. Returns ``(message_text, reasoning_content, tool_calls)``.
    """
    message_parts: list[str] = []
    reasoning_parts: list[str] = []
    tool_calls: list[ToolCall] = []
    for item in message.get("output") or []:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue  # tolerate a malformed item rather than drop the trajectory
        item_type = item.get("type")
        if item_type == "message":
            text = _normalize_content(item.get("content"))
            if text:
                message_parts.append(text)
        elif item_type == "reasoning":
            # GPT-5.x reasoning text is usually encrypted (empty summary/content).
            for key in ("summary", "content"):
                value = item.get(key)
                if not isinstance(value, list):
                    continue
                for part in value:
                    text = part.get("text") if isinstance(part, dict) else None
                    if text:
                        reasoning_parts.append(text)
        elif item_type == "function_call":
            tool_calls.append(
                ToolCall(
                    tool_call_id=item.get("call_id")
                    or item.get("id")
                    or f"call_{step_id}_{len(tool_calls) + 1}",
                    function_name=item.get("name", "bash"),
                    arguments=_normalize_tool_args(item.get("arguments", "{}")),
                )
            )
    return (
        "\n".join(message_parts),
        "\n".join(reasoning_parts) or None,
        tool_calls or None,
    )
